thread:
Samir Patel: Hey team — GlacierPay (acct: glacierpay-acc-21) on Dedicated pool dp-45 is hitting sustained TPS spikes since ~03:10 UTC. We're seeing token-per-second SLO violations and 429s. Burst credits went to 0 repeatedly and admission control is oscillating between allow/reject. Need triage.

Joanne Li: ACK. Can you paste pool id and any quick logs?

Samir Patel: pool-id: dp-45. Recent admission log snippet below (sanitized):
```
03:09:58 ADMISSION pool=dp-45 acct=glacierpay-acc-21 req_qps=850 tps_window=60 credits=18 -> allow
03:10:12 ADMISSION pool=dp-45 acct=glacierpay-acc-21 req_qps=1720 tps_window=60 credits=18 -> consume->0 -> allowuntil=03:10:12
03:10:13 ADMISSION pool=dp-45 acct=glacierpay-acc-21 req_qps=1801 credits=0 -> reject 429
03:10:35 ADMISSION pool=dp-45 acct=glacierpay-acc-21 req_qps=900 credits=0 -> reject 429
```
Looks like rapid oscillation when burst credits are exhausted.

Chris Nguyen: Pulling metrics — autoscaler has stayed at 4 GPUs (target min=4,max=12). I don't see new nodes registering. Kube events show no scale-up triggered. GPU utilization is uneven: node-2 shows low GPU load but high memory for KV cache (per-tenant cache growth). Could be noisy-neighbor blocking effective capacity.

Kieran O'Riley: @Chris can you run `redwoodctl pools describe dp-45 --metrics 03:00-03:20` and `kubectl get nodes -o wide` from the control plane? Also check admission-controller logs: `kubectl logs -n redwood admission-controller-xxxxx`

Chris Nguyen: Ran describe output (trimmed):
- pool dp-45: provisioned_gpus=4, in_use=4, pending_scale_up=false, avg_latency_p50=120ms, p95=340ms, tps=~1.6K
- queue_depth spiked 3x around 03:10
kubectl shows 0 pending nodes and autoscaler reported scale decision suppressed due to utilization imbalance: "scale-suppressed: nodegroup dp-45: podAff/antiAff conflicts"

Joanne Li: Hmm pod affinity conflicts — did the recent scheduler tweak roll out?

deploy-bot: rollout admission-controller v2.4.1 -> v2.4.2 at 03:05 UTC (canary 10%).

Samir Patel: That rollout coincides with the spike window. Could be a behavior/regression. Worth rolling back the admission change if parity shows.

Kieran O'Riley: I'm seeing admission-controller metrics: token_bucket_replenish_latency spiked and token_drain_rate increased after v2.4.2 canary. Possible bug in credit accounting when multiple concurrent inflight requests with large initial token debt.

Chris Nguyen: I can reproduce locally against a mirror cluster: send 2x baseline QPS burst (scripts attached) and the admission-controller consumed credits incorrectly when many concurrent new sessions open with large initial context sizes. Repro curl snippet: `for i in {1..600}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d'{"model":"rdw-2b","input": "payload-${i}", "max_tokens":400}'; done` — this drives large token issuance and trips the bug.

Joanne Li: Customer reports the spike originates from a scheduled marketing campaign hitting their front-end at 03:09 UTC. They scaled clients unintentionally.

Maria Ortiz: We should offer temporary relief. Options: 1) increase burst credits for glacierpay-acc-21, 2) adjust admission thresholds, or 3) ask them to throttle. Any risk to other tenants if we bump credits?

Kieran O'Riley: Increasing per-account burst credits on a shared pool risks starving other tenants if autoscale is suppressed. Short term we can: a) add a temporary per-account emergency credit (soft cap) with monitoring, b) enable per-tenant KV cache eviction heuristic to free memory, c) rollback admission-controller canary to v2.4.1. I recommend rollback + KV eviction + ask customer to throttle.

Chris Nguyen: Rolling back canary on admission-controller now (started 03:30 UTC). Patch note: revert token accounting tweak.

deploy-bot: rollback admission-controller to v2.4.1 initiated by chris_nguyen at 03:31 UTC — canary reduced to 0%.

Samir Patel: While rollback is in progress, can we apply a temporary per-account credit bump (expires 1h) so GlacierPay's endpoints recover? They are seeing production errors in payments.

Maria Ortiz: I can approve an emergency +50% burst credit for 1 hour for glacierpay-acc-21 if eng guarantees monitoring and a rollback plan. Please add incident ticket and note expected cost.

Kieran O'Riley: Created INC-2026-2298 and attached runbook steps. I'll enable eviction heuristic on dp-45 and set a watch for queue_depth and token_bucket_consumption.

Chris Nguyen: Bumped credits for glacierpay-acc-21 by +50% at 03:36 UTC (expires 04:36 UTC). Monitoring shows credits no longer hitting zero and 429s drop sharply. Autoscaler still suppressed until we fix pod affinity issue but rollback reduces token drain.

Samir Patel: Customer confirmed error rate dropped from 8% -> 0.6% after credits bump and rollback. They're happy for now but request a root cause writeup.

Joanne Li: Actions: 1) Eng to root cause token accounting regression in admission v2.4.2 (Kieran/Chris). 2) Fix pod affinity rules to allow scale-ups (Chris). 3) Update KB for ops on emergency credit bump and eviction toggle (Joanne/Maria). 4) Follow up with GlacierPay billing note for emergency credits (Maria).

Kieran O'Riley: Root cause summary so far (short): v2.4.2 introduced a change to initial token reservation for new sessions which double-counted some inflight handshake tokens under concurrency; combined with a suppressed autoscaler (affinity regression) and per-tenant KV cache growth this starved effective serving capacity and exhausted burst credits. Working on a unit/regression test and a patched release.

Maria Ortiz: Billing: mark the emergency credit as "ops-relief" pending customer approval for charge. I'll send a bill hold/notice to GlacierPay and CC support.

Chris Nguyen: Patch branch created to fix reservation double-counting. Will run staged canary after we fix scheduler affinity bug and add regression tests. ETA for stable patch 6 hours.

Samir Patel: Great work. I'll keep the customer looped in and schedule a postmortem in #postmortems tomorrow. Closing internal triage — will update INC-2026-2298 with final RCA and cost impact. :thumbsup:

Joanne Li: Thanks everyone.
